summary: Abandoned summit lookout north of Lillooet; trip reports describe its condition, but no source gives a build date or staffing history.

facts.status_note: Abandoned. Trip reports describe a derelict building with no windows left.

access.note: A hike route to the summit is described in the directory entry and trip reports. No source describes a closure or a permit for the lookout.

visit.trail_note: Trail starts across the road from a cattle guard, off the rugged West Pavilion road. The first part follows a decommissioned road; the last section is loose, slippery and steep.

events.note: Directory describes an old abandoned forestry fire lookout at the summit; OpenStreetMap tags it abandoned. No date given.
Peak and range named after camels; the directory credits John Calbreath with the 1862 experiment, while a trip report and Wikipedia credit the purchase to Frank Laumeister.

Trip report found a few remains of an old TV and radio antenna and building at the first lookout, a treeless knob southwest of Camelshoof Peak; the directory says the old transmission site has no structures left.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia places an old forestry lookout on an unnamed pinnacle upriver near North Fountain; the directory and a trip report put it on the summit ridge. The story reports both and describes the summit lookout the directory and trip report describe.
The directory credits John Calbreath; a trip report and Wikipedia credit Frank Laumeister. All three give 23 camels, and the directory and trip report give 1862. The story reports both names.

notes_for_editor: No build date, height, design or staffing found in any readable source. Firelookout.ca shows N/A for year built and tower type. Status standing rests on the undated directory entry, OpenStreetMap, and a trip report dated May 17, 2015 (ashikaparsad.com); no date was found for the awalkandalark report, which is the only source for the no-windows note. Access was 'unknown' in the brief; public is inferred from the hike route, with no closure notice found. The BC Wildfire Service attribution comes only from OpenStreetMap. The lookout location conflict (Wikipedia pinnacle vs summit) is unresolved and should be checked against a map before publishing.
